  Readable gloss: "Built from hypo ('under') and meno ('remain'), this verb pictures someone who stands firm under a heavy load rather than fleeing. Yet the compound's older spatial meaning — 'to stay behind after others have left' — surfaces twice: the boy Jesus remaining behind in Jerusalem (Luke 2:43) and Silas staying in Berea when Paul departs (Acts 17:14). Spanish permanecer in these cases signals the purely locative sense, distinct from the moral fortitude implied elsewhere."
